layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: When visiting a place, for example while traveling, we often want

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to capture the moment, to help us remember what it was like to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be in that place. Most of us capture a handful of photos with our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: smartphones for this reason, but the sense of immersion is lost when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: played back as a sequence of stills – the sense of the scale of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: space is missing. We can create a single view that extends beyond

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the field-of-view of the camera by stitching multiple exposures into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a panoramic image. Many video cameras can automatically stitch

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the frames of a panning video into a panoramic still image, so long

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as the scene is static. While we can capture a space with an image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: panorama, however, the experience of the dynamic scene in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moment, filled with moving people, cars, trees, water, etc., is lost.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we propose to construct panoramic videos from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: casually-captured panning video of general dynamic scenes, com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pleting both the space and time spanned by the panoramic video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volume. We take as input a video that can include not just a single

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pan, but multiple pans in one capture, e.g., panning from left to right

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and then back left again. In this more general multi-pan setting, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have both an opportunity to ground the video with knowledge of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: what happened later" as we pan back to a spatial location at a later

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time, but also the challenge of consistently interpolating across gaps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in time to answer the question “what happened in between?"

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our approach is to register the input video frames into a sin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gle video volume, leaving space-time regions outside of the input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unknown, then complete the unknown volume regions. This task

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is challenging since in a typical capture, the number of unknown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixels in this volume outnumbers the known pixels, and we can-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not assume that the unknown regions are stationary. To solve this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: problem we need a powerful and realistic prior model of video,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a method to apply this prior to complete the video volume

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistently. We demonstrate results with both a diffusion-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model (Lumiere [Bar-Tal et al. 2024]) and a token-based model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Phenaki [Villegas et al. 2022]). The main technical problem we ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dress is how to constrain and condition these video generation mod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: els, which have limited context windows, to complete a panoramic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video of arbitrary length and width. To tackle this challenge we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: apply coarse-to-fine synthesis and spatial aggregation techniques

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to realistically and consistently complete unknown regions of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video volume.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In summary, our contributions include:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The first system for creating video panoramas from general, pan-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ning input videos that include moving people and objects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Adaptations of the base algorithm for diffusion- and token-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video generation models, and an analysis of their relative strengths

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and weaknesses.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • A new dataset of video panoramas (cropped from 360-degree

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: videos) with synthetic panning camera motion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1 Image Panorama Stitching

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A long line of work has focused on the problem of panorama stitch-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing [Brown and Lowe 2007; Shum and Szeliski 1997; Steedly et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2005; Szeliski et al. 2007; Szeliski and Shum 2000; Xiong and Pulli

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2010], i.e., simulating a wider field-of-view image from a set of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images captured by a camera rotating in place. These methods typi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cally involve a series of steps including (1) sparse feature-based or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semi-dense registration [Lowe 2004], (2) rigid or depth-compensated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alignment, and (3) image blending [Burt and Adelson 1987; Gracias

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. 2009; Pérez et al. 2023], to resolve seams and inconsistencies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: across observations. A major failure mode of image panorama ac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quisition is in scenes with dynamic objects—since significant scene

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: motion can cause failures in both registration and compositing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.2 Video Panoramas

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The limitation of image stitching in handling moving objects has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been explored in a series of work expanding image panoramas to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the video domain [Agarwala et al. 2005; Couture et al. 2011; Rav-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Acha et al. 2007]. Commonly referred to as panoramic video textures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these methods use a graph-cut formulation to solve the panorama

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: blending problem across both spatially and temporally varying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observations, and are able to produce panoramas with motion that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can even loop seamlessly [Liao et al. 2015, 2013]. Still, these methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are restricted to modeling textural motion, e.g. shaking trees and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flowing water, and cannot resolve inconsistencies resulting from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transient objects, e.g. a person walking across the scene. This is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: largely due to the fact that these methods do not generate novel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observations of the scene—rather, their goal is to consolidate existing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observations into a consistent representation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.3 Video Completion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Video completion focuses on completing missing pixels given ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: served pixels as context. Many methods retrieve visual features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g. pixels, patches, segments, templates, proposals) from the ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: served regions to fill in the missing regions [Gao et al. 2020; Hu et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2020; Huang et al. 2016; Ilan and Shamir 2015; Li et al. 2022; Wexler

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. 2007; Zhou et al. 2023]. However, these methods tend to fail

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or produce low-fidelity results when the observation is sparse or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: incomplete (e.g. heavily-masked video, object insertion).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: With recent advances in generative models [Bar-Tal et al. 2024;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Blattmann et al. 2023a,b; Guo et al. 2023; Ho et al. 2022; Villegas et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2022; Zhou et al. 2022], many methods adapt pretrained generative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models for the task of video completion [Bar-Tal et al. 2024; Zhang

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. 2023] or train versatile generative models on a suite of tasks,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where video completion is one of them [Kondratyuk et al. 2024;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Yu et al. 2023]. While the generative completion methods succeed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on a broader range of scenarios (e.g. foreground/background re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: placement, transient motion), they fail on the task of panoramic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video completion, which requires going beyond the model's tem-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poral and spatial context window, interpolating temporally-distant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observations and completing regions under a panning video mask.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 Method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The input to the method is a video captured with a panning camera

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that sweeps over a scene containing moving people and objects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The output is a complete panoramic video of the same duration as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the input, but spatially wide enough to capture the entire sweep of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the input camera (e.g., Fig. 1). The output panoramic video should

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: match the input video in the known input regions, and should look

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: realistic and consistent. Since the extent of the unknown content

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may span a significant portion of the video in both time and space,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we harness the power of a generative video prior to synthesize the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: missing regions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While existing text-to-video models encode powerful priors about

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our dynamic world, a pivotal challenge in utilizing them for our task

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is their limited spatio-temporal context window. We overcome this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: restriction by adopting a coarse-to-fine approach in the temporal di-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mension and mask-respecting aggregation in the spatial dimension

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Fig. 2). To ensure consistent motion across time, we first temporally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: downsample the video to the model's context window length and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complete a base panoramic video by aggregating the model predic-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions in sliding spatial windows (Sec. 3.3). We then progressively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: restore the temporal details by temporal upsampling, merging with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the input video, and resynthesizing pixels outside the input regions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Sec. 3.4). Optionally, the model may be finetuned at test-time to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: further improve fidelity of the completed video (Sec. 3.5).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1 Preliminaries: Video Generation Models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To illustrate the generality of the method, we employ two video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generation models in our experiments: Lumiere [Bar-Tal et al. 2024]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Phenaki [Villegas et al. 2022]. Lumiere is a space-time, pixel-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diffusion model with a two-stage cascade: a base model that pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duces 80 frames of 128 × 128 pixels, followed by an upsampling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stage to 1024 × 1024 pixels. Phenaki is a token-based model with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an encoder/decoder pair to translate between pixels and the latent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: token space, as well as a two-stage cascade: first 11 frames of 160×96

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixels, then 320 × 192 pixels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2 Video Registration and Setup

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the remaining sections we use the following notation for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intermediate variables:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To prepare a video for processing we project the input video onto

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a panoramic canvas to produce input frames

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and corresponding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask frames of valid pixels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the panorama coordinate system.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For videos with pure panning camera motion (rotation only), we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can use a fast, standard homography solver [Hartley and Zisserman

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2004]. When camera parallax is present, we solve for a full 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: camera path using a more expensive, robust SLAM system [Zhang

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. 2022]. We ignore the translation of the camera and compute

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the elevation θ and azimuth

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of each input pixel's ray relative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the first frame's camera direction, then project each ray to an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equirectangular canvas.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We further prepare temporally-downsampled versions of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such that the coarsest input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fits exactly in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model's context window (80 frames for Lumiere, 11 for Phenaki).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 3.5 Inference-Time Finetuning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Some modules of the video generation model can be optionally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: finetuned at inference time to further improve results. The Phenaki

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model's encoder/decoder architecture in particular incurs some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fidelity loss, so the base Phenaki model cannot exactly reproduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the original video pixels. To better align the result with the input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video, we finetune the Phenaki decoder dec on patches of valid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixels x  m prior to synthesizing the final result. Finetuning helps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to preserve details of the input in the outpainted regions. Lumiere is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a pixel-diffusion model without an encoder and decoder step, and we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found it produced results closer to the input video overall, though

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high-frequency details could likely be improved with finetuning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (see Sec. 5).

layout_dets.text: 4 Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We evaluate our approach in two settings: real-world casual panning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: captures, and “synthetic” panning videos generated by applying a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moving crop window to videos captured with a 360-degree camera.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The synthetic setting allows us to compare the models' performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: directly against a ground-truth panoramic video.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.1 Baseline Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We include four baseline methods for comparison (Fig. 5): a simple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: linear interpolation baseline, two flow-based video inpainting al-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gorithms, and a recent video generation model MAGVIT [Yu et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2023] that demonstrated video panorama outpainting.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Linear interpolation baseline. For the linear baseline, the output

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: color at pixel p is a linear interpolation of the closest before and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: after frames, or the nearest neighbor frame if only before or after

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exists. The result matches the input video exactly and matches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: any stationary elements in the scene. Moving objects exhibit the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expected ghosting artifacts, with extreme failures in the case of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: non-stationary camera.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Flow-based baselines. We include two methods for video inpaint-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing using optical flow: ProPainter [Zhou et al. 2023] and E²FGVI[Li

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. 2022]. These methods are tasked with completing the region

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outside the valid pixels m. Both methods internally estimate flow,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: so the only inputs are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MAGVIT baseline. For the MAGVIT baseline, we apply repeated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: horizontal outpainting to extend the input video to outside the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: panorama canvas, then crop. Due to the temporal window of MAGVIT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: being limited to 16 frames, we subsample a portion of each video to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: obtain a single-direction pan of the full scene from left to right, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluate only on this subset of frames.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.2 Quantitative Evaluation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Besides typical similarity metrics (PSNR, LPIPS [Zhang et al. 2018])

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and single-video FID [Arora and Lee 2021], we also compute optical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flow EPE (endpoint error) to measure the consistency of the gener-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ated motions. We compute flow between consecutive frames of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: groundtruth and the output video and measure their L2 difference.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: When evaluating small motions at low image resolution, we empiri-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cally found grid-based flow [Szeliski 2010] to produce more reliable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sub-pixel alignments than network-based flow (e.g. RAFT [Teed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Deng 2020]). For pixel-level metrics (PSNR, EPE), we separately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluate static and dynamic regions (see supplemental for details).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.3 Synthetic Panning Videos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To create synthetic panning videos we center crop an input video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: captured with a 360-degree video camera and add a moving crop

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: window over 88 frames at 15fps (Figure 7). We then apply our system

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to complete a new video panorama. We curated 12 360-degree videos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: licensed under Creative Commons and plan to include these videos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: along with our results upon publication.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Synthetic videos allow us to evaluate the model's output directly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: against a ground-truth video panorama. Note that our goal is to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generate a plausible completed panorama, not recreate an input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: panorama. However, our model should recreate stationary scene

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elements as closely as possible.

layout_dets.text: Besides the alternative baselines, we analyze two main ablations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of temporal coarse-to-fine. Ablation results are shown in Fig. 9 and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model was trained on static masks, it produces significant artifacts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the dynamic-mask panorama videos, including visible seams

layout_dets.text: 5 Discussion and Limitations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The method presented in this paper can complete a panoramic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video from a casually-captured panning video. This task would be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impossible without a strong prior on realistic videos and motion,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which has only recently become available in the form of generative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models of video. While panoramic videos from stationary (rotation-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only), panning cameras have been shown in limited settings, such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as Panoramic Video Textures [Agarwala et al. 2005], constructing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: panoramic videos containing large object motions (Fig. 1) or the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entirely shifting visual field of a moving camera (Fig. 8, "dynibar")

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are capabilities unlocked only with a generative video prior.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Given the nascent capabilities of generative video models, however,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our method has some limitations that could lead to future work:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Limited context window. Current video generation models pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cess a limited number of frames simultaneously (80 for Lumiere,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 11 for Phenaki). This limited context window necessitates a tempo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ral coarse-to-fine approach to allow the model to fill in the entire

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: panoramic video consistently (Fig. 10). A limited amount of tem-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poral coarsening is possible, however, without completely blurring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: out fast motion or dropping small objects. For our experiments we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used up to 5 levels of temporal coarsening for Phenaki and 2 for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Lumiere, for a maximum video length of 172 or 160 frames.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Synthesis quality. While the quality of the generated video is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: often convincing, neither model we tested consistently generates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: photorealistic results. Limitations on synthesis quality are espe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cially noticeable for close-up human faces (e.g., Fig. 10, "palace")

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our diffusion-based results could potentially preserve the high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frequencies of the input videos better by finetuning the Lumiere

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: super-resolution module with mask-conditioning. However, this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modification would require adding a new conditioning input and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computationally-intensive retraining, and was not done as part of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this work. We expect this limitation to be removed in the future.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Latent video diffusion models. Several recent video generation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models [Blattmann et al. 2023a; Guo et al. 2023] use a latent diffu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion model (LDM) as a backbone to reduce runtime cost. Since the
